subject: Re: Pricing for new embedding-heavy workloads and burst capacity
messages:
From: Liam Turner <liam@brightmetrics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New product line — pricing question (embedding-heavy / burst)

Hi Grace,

Quick question — we're spinning up a new feature that will call embeddings for short context (up to 256 tokens) but at much higher QPS than our current workloads (estimated 3–5x peak). We expect steady monthly usage of ~30B tokens for generation and ~120M embedding calls (avg 40 tokens each).

Two asks:
- Can you share how per-token volume discounts map to commit tiers for Hosted API? We were quoted a baseline per-token list earlier but need clarity on incremental commit paths (e.g., add-on workloads vs. new teams).
- We also need short bursts (spikes 10–15x for short windows). Does Redwood support burst credits or a short-term bump without moving to Dedicated?

Happy to jump on 30 mins — CC'ing procurement for PO questions.

Thanks,
Liam
VP Product, BrightMetrics
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam@brightmetrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New product line — pricing question (embedding-heavy / burst)

Hi Liam — great to hear about the new feature, congrats.

Short answers up front: yes, we can do incremental commits and we offer burst capacity on Hosted via temporary "burst credits" tied to committed tiers (no mandatory Dedicated move). I attached a one-page MAP and the current pricing grid so you can see the tier breakpoints.

How the incremental path usually works (summary):
- Baseline commit: set a monthly token commit for Hosted API that unlocks per-token discount bands.
- Add-on workloads: you can add workloads under the same commit and they inherit the discount; if usage materially changes (10%+ of total), we revisit the banding.
- Incremental commit: you can add a top-up commit mid-term — we model blended pricing for the remainder of the term and set the new commit start date.
- Burst credits: available as a short-term credit pool purchasable at a fixed uplift; automatically consumed before dipping into on-demand.

I'll let Ben propose numbers based on your forecast and the MAP.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben will send a draft incremental-commit proposal with blended rates + burst credit pricing.
2) If procurement is happy, we'll issue a short MAP and a DocuSign PO amendment for the top-up.

Attaching: Redwood_MAP_v3.pdf, pricing_grid_v2.xlsx

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam@brightmetrics.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Incremental commit + burst credit proposal (numbers)

Hi Liam — following up with proposed numbers based on your forecast (30B gen tokens / 120M embeddings @ ~40 tokens):

Proposal (12-month amendment):
- Incremental commit: +36B gen tokens/mo (covers expected growth and variance) and +5M embedding units/mo (embedding units = calls * avg tokens).
- Pricing: blended per-token equivalent at $0.0009/gen-token after commit (effective across baseline + incremental). Embeddings priced at $0.00075/embedding-token equivalent.
- Burst credits: sellable pool equal to 20% of committed throughput per month. Burst credit consumption priced at a 35% uplift to committed per-token rates.
- Minimum incremental term: 6 months for the top-up, billable monthly, with an option to convert to annual committed pricing at month 6.

Why this structure: it preserves your ability to keep workloads on Hosted API (no immediate Dedicated move), gives predictable unit economics, and keeps a clear conversion path if you decide to lock in higher commit for long-term discounts.

Action items:
- If you approve, we'll generate a MAP with exact quantities and numbers for your procurement team to sign (I attached the draft MAP & pricing grid).
- Sergio, can you confirm the burst credit enforcement and the max sustainable QPS assumptions for a 20% burst pool?

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: pricing_grid_v2.xlsx, Redwood_MAP_v3.pdf

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Liam Turner <liam@brightmetrics.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incremental commit + burst credit proposal (numbers)

Thanks — quick technical confirmation on burst pool behavior and capacity planning:

- Burst credits are enforced at the account routing layer. Traffic consumes burst credits first; once exhausted, requests fall back to on-demand at the uplifted rate or are rate-limited based on your routing policy.
- For the 20% pool on your proposed commit, we model safe sustained spikes up to ~8–10x for short windows (90s–10m) depending on sequence length; sustained multi-hour spikes >3x will start to exhaust the pool.
- For embedding-heavy calls: because call size is short, KV-prefix caching and batching will improve efficiency; we'll dedicate an embedding-optimized kernel on your shard which we expect to lower per-token latency and reduce effective cost by ~5–8% vs on-demand without changing pricing bands.

Next steps from my side: I will add a short technical appendix to the MAP describing burst enforcement and expected token/run-rate behavior. Ben — once you get PO language back, send the DocuSign link and I’ll confirm the routing config and shard sizing.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
